title: Jira Review 2026: Is Atlassian's AI-Powered Project Management Still the Gold Standard?
content:

## Quick Answer

**Jira Software** by Atlassian is the most widely adopted project management and issue-tracking platform in the world — and in 2026, it has evolved far beyond bug tracking. With the Spring 2026 release introducing **AI agents powered by Rovo**, MCP integration for AI coding tools like Cursor and Claude Code, and the new **Teamwork Graph** for cross-team visibility, Jira is positioning itself as the operating system for AI-augmented software teams. It's used by over 300,000 organizations including NASA, Tesla, Spotify, and Airbnb. Plans start at **$0 for up to 10 users** (Free forever), with Standard at **$7.91/user/month** and Premium at **$14.54/user/month**. Jira is undeniably powerful — but it comes with a learning curve that smaller teams and non-technical users may find overwhelming. If your team ships software at scale and you want AI agents working alongside your developers, Jira is the platform to beat in 2026.

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Industry-leading AI agents** — Rovo AI agents can auto-triage bugs, generate PR descriptions, summarize sprints, and even assign tasks based on developer workload and expertise
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration** — AI coding assistants like Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Codex can update Jira issues directly from the CLI, closing the gap between the IDE and the project tracker
- **Unmatched flexibility** — Custom workflows, issue types, fields, screens, and permissions let you model literally any software development process (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, hybrid)
- **3,000+ integrations** — Deep native integrations with Slack, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Figma, Google Docs, Microsoft Teams, and hundreds more
- **Powerful automation engine** — No-code automation rules that handle everything from auto-assigning PR reviewers to escalating stale issues; 100 free automations/month on Free plan, scaling to unlimited on Enterprise
- **Teamwork Graph** — New cross-team visibility feature shows dependencies, bottlenecks, and delivery health across your entire organization in a single graph view
- **Enterprise-grade security** — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR compliant, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and 99.95% uptime SLA on Enterprise
- **Free tier that actually works** — Free plan for up to 10 users includes unlimited goals, projects, tasks, backlog, boards, timelines, and calendars — generous enough for startups and small teams

### Cons 👎

- **Steep learning curve** — The sheer configurability that makes Jira powerful also makes it intimidating; first-time admins can easily over-engineer workflows, and new team members often need 1-2 weeks to feel productive
- **UI can feel cluttered** — Despite the 2024-2026 redesign efforts, the interface still packs a lot of information density; compared to Linear, Notion, or Monday.com, Jira can feel less polished visually
- **Per-user pricing adds up** — At $14.54/user/month on Premium, a 50-person team costs $727/month ($8,724/year); this is reasonable for enterprise but steep for bootstrapped startups
- **Admin overhead is real** — Someone needs to own Jira administration; without a dedicated admin, configurations drift, permission schemes become a maze, and the instance can degrade into chaos
- **Mobile experience lags** — The Jira mobile app is functional for triaging and approving but lacks the full power of the desktop experience; power users will feel constrained
- **No free domain or hosting** — Compared to all-in-one platforms, Jira doesn't bundle complementary services; you'll still need separate tools for documentation (Confluence), code (Bitbucket/GitHub), and communication (Slack/Teams)

---

## Full Review

### What Is Jira Software in 2026?

Jira started in 2002 as a bug-tracking tool for software developers. Fast-forward 24 years and it has become the nervous system for how software gets built at companies ranging from 10-person startups to Fortune 50 enterprises. In 2026, Atlassian's vision for Jira has crystallized around three pillars: **AI-augmented workflows**, **open ecosystem integration** (the MCP standard), and **cross-team orchestration** via the Teamwork Graph.

The Spring 2026 release marks an inflection point. For the first time, Jira ships with **Rovo AI agents** that operate autonomously within your projects — they can scan your backlog for duplicate issues, auto-generate sprint retrospectives from commit data, triage incoming bugs by severity, and even suggest code reviewers based on git blame history. This isn't just AI in a chatbot sidebar; it's AI embedded in the workflow itself.

Atlassian has also embraced the Model Context Protocol (MCP), originally developed by Anthropic, as the standard for connecting AI coding tools to Jira. This means when a developer in Cursor or Claude Code resolves a bug, the corresponding Jira ticket gets updated automatically — no manual status changes, no context switching. For teams already using AI-assisted development in 2026, this integration alone can save 30-60 minutes per developer per day.

### Who Is Jira For?

Jira is purpose-built for **software development teams** — but its flexibility has expanded its use case dramatically. Here's a breakdown of who benefits most:

**Ideal for:**
- **Enterprise software teams** running Scrum, Kanban, or SAFe at scale with 50-5,000+ developers
- **DevOps and platform engineering teams** tracking infrastructure work, incidents, and SRE toil alongside feature development
- **Agencies and consultancies** that need to track billable hours, client-specific workflows, and cross-project resource allocation
- **Product management organizations** managing complex roadmaps with dependencies across multiple squads
- **AI-native development teams** using Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or Copilot and wanting seamless IDE-to-Jira integration via MCP

**Not ideal for:**
- **Solo founders or freelancers** — Jira is overkill; Todoist, Linear, or even Notion are better fits
- **Non-technical teams** (marketing, HR, legal) — While Jira can work for these teams, tools like Asana, Monday.com, or ClickUp offer friendlier onboarding
- **Teams that value simplicity over configurability** — If you want a tool that "just works" out of the box, Linear or Basecamp will make you happier

### Pricing: What Does Jira Cost in 2026?

Atlassian's pricing model is per-user, per-month with monthly and annual billing options (annual saves up to 17%). Here's the complete breakdown as of August 2026:

| Plan | Monthly Price (per user) | Annual Price (per user) | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | $0 | $0 | Teams of up to 10; unlimited goals, projects, tasks, backlog, board, timeline, calendar, and summary views; 100 automations/month; 2 GB storage; Community support |
| **Standard** | $7.91 | $6.58 (save ~17%) | Growing teams; adds Rovo AI Search, Chat, and Agents; user roles and permissions; external collaboration; 1,700 automations/month; 250 GB storage; 9/5 regional support; up to 100,000 users |
| **Premium** | $14.54 | $12.10 (save ~17%) | Multi-team organizations; adds cross-team planning and dependency management; customizable approvals; per-user automation (1,000 runs/user/month); unlimited storage; 24/7 critical support; 99.9% uptime SLA |
| **Enterprise** | Contact sales (annual only) | Contact sales | Large enterprises; adds Atlassian Analytics and Data Lake; advanced admin controls; enterprise IAM; unlimited automations; up to 150 sites; 24/7 all-issue support; 99.95% uptime SLA |

**Real-world cost examples:**
- **10-person startup (Free)**: $0/month — generous but limited to 2 GB storage and 100 automations
- **25-person team (Standard, monthly)**: $197.75/month ($2,373/year)
- **50-person engineering org (Premium, annual)**: $605/month ($7,260/year)
- **200-person enterprise (Enterprise, annual)**: Typically $25,000-$45,000/year depending on negotiated volume pricing

**Cost-saving tips:**
- Always choose annual billing for the ~17% discount
- The Free plan is genuinely useful for small teams — don't upgrade until you hit the 10-user or 2 GB limit
- Enterprise pricing includes Confluence and Jira Service Management in many bundles — negotiate the full suite
- Cloud migration from Server/Data Center often comes with promotional pricing for the first year

### AI Features: Rovo Agents and MCP Integration

The 2026 AI capabilities are Jira's most transformative feature set in years. Here's what's actually useful versus what's marketing fluff:

**Rovo AI Agents (Game-changer ⭐)**
Rovo is Atlassian's answer to the AI agent revolution. In Jira, Rovo agents can:
- **Auto-triage incoming bugs**: Rovo reads the bug description, checks your knowledge base and past resolved issues, suggests severity and component labels, and can even propose assignees based on code ownership data
- **Generate sprint retrospectives**: After a sprint closes, Rovo analyzes commit messages, PR descriptions, and issue transitions to produce a draft retrospective — including what went well, what got blocked, and velocity trends
- **Smart backlog grooming**: Rovo identifies duplicate issues, flags stale tickets (no updates in 30+ days), and suggests story point estimates based on historical data from similar issues
- **PR description generation**: When a developer creates a PR, Rovo can auto-generate the description from linked Jira issues, including acceptance criteria and test cases

**MCP (Model Context Protocol) Integration (Developer-focused ✨)**
The MCP integration is what makes Jira truly AI-native in 2026. Any AI coding tool that supports MCP — Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf — can interact with Jira directly:
```
# Example: Claude Code updates a Jira ticket from the terminal
> "Mark NDS-1234 as In Review and add a comment with the PR link"
[Claude Code calls Jira MCP server → ticket updated instantly]
```
This eliminates one of the biggest sources of developer friction: context switching between the IDE and the project tracker. Early adopters report saving 2-5 hours per developer per week on administrative Jira updates alone.

**AI-Powered Search and Summarization**
Rovo Search, included from Standard upward, uses semantic search across your entire Atlassian instance (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket). Instead of remembering exact issue keys, you can search with natural language: "What was the database migration issue from last month that caused the outage?" and Rovo finds the relevant tickets, Confluence pages, and code commits.

### Core Project Management Features

**Scrum and Kanban Boards**
Jira's boards are the heart of the product, and they've matured significantly. Scrum boards support sprint planning, velocity charts, burn-down/burn-up reports, and capacity planning. Kanban boards offer WIP (Work In Progress) limits, cumulative flow diagrams, and control charts for cycle time analysis. The 2026 update introduced **board templates by team type** — engineering, design, marketing, and IT operations — each pre-configured with relevant issue types, workflows, and metrics.

**Backlog Management**
The backlog view supports drag-and-drop prioritization, epic grouping, version assignment, and bulk operations. The new **AI-assisted backlog ranking** (Premium+) uses historical velocity, dependency chains, and business priority to suggest optimal sprint sequencing — essentially an auto-prioritization engine.

**Roadmaps (Basic and Advanced)**
- **Basic Roadmaps** (Standard+): Single-team timeline view for planning 1-3 months ahead
- **Advanced Roadmaps** (Premium+): Cross-team, multi-quarter planning with capacity management, scenario planning, and what-if analysis

**Custom Workflows**
This is Jira's superpower and its biggest trap. You can model any process — from a simple "To Do → In Progress → Done" to multi-step approval workflows with conditions, validators, and post-functions triggered by specific transitions. The trap: without governance, teams create byzantine workflows with 15+ statuses that nobody understands. The new **workflow template library** (2026) and **AI workflow suggestions** (Premium+) help mitigate this.

**Automation**
Jira's no-code automation engine is genuinely excellent. It uses a trigger → condition → action model:
- **Trigger**: Issue created, field changed, sprint started, etc.
- **Condition**: JQL query, user in group, field matches regex, etc.
- **Action**: Assign issue, transition status, send Slack message, create sub-tasks, etc.

The automation library has 200+ pre-built templates like "Auto-close stale issues after 14 days" or "Auto-assign based on component." The new **AI automation suggestions** (Premium+) analyze your project history and propose automations — for example, if it notices PRs consistently get merged 2 days after code review approval, it might suggest auto-closing the corresponding Jira ticket on merge.

### Reporting and Analytics

Jira ships with 30+ built-in reports, and the quality varies significantly by plan:

| Report Type | Free | Standard | Premium | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Burn-down/Burn-up Charts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Velocity Chart | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Cumulative Flow Diagram | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Control Chart | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Version/Epic Reports | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Sprint Retrospective Report (AI) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Cross-Project Reports | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Atlassian Analytics (Data Lake) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

**Dashboards** are highly customizable with 20+ gadget types (issue statistics, pie charts, heat maps, sprint health, etc.). You can create multiple dashboards per project and share them with stakeholders who don't have Jira accounts via **public links** (Premium+).

The Enterprise plan's **Atlassian Analytics** with Data Lake is worth highlighting — it lets you run SQL queries across all your Atlassian products (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket) to answer questions like "What's the average time from code review approval to production deployment across all teams this quarter?"

### Integrations and Ecosystem

Jira's 3,000+ integrations are a key reason enterprises choose it. The Atlassian Marketplace is a $2B+ ecosystem with apps for time tracking (Tempo, Clockify), test management (Xray, Zephyr), design (Figma, InVision), CI/CD (Jenkins, CircleCI, GitHub Actions), and hundreds more.

Key native integrations:
- **Slack**: Real-time Jira notifications, slash commands to create/transition issues, and the new AI-powered `/jira ask` that queries your instance via Rovo
- **GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket**: Smart commits (`NDS-1234 #done` in a commit message transitions the issue), branch creation from issues, deployment tracking
- **Figma**: Embed design files directly in issues; designers get notified when implementation status changes
- **Microsoft Teams**: Bi-directional sync with the Jira Cloud app for Teams
- **Google Docs**: Embed live Jira issues in Docs; changes to issue status update in real-time

### Ease of Use: The Elephant in the Room

Let's be direct: Jira is harder to use than its competitors. This is both its greatest strength and its most common criticism. Jira's 4.2/5 G2 rating (6,000+ reviews) and 4.4/5 Capterra rating (14,000+ reviews) reflect this duality — users love the power but resent the complexity.

**Where the friction comes from:**
1. **Configuration overload**: New admins face a blank canvas with infinite possibilities; without clear guidance, they over-configure
2. **Permission scheme complexity**: Jira's permission model is powerful (project-level, issue-level, field-level) but notoriously difficult to debug when something goes wrong
3. **Terminology opacity**: "Resolved" vs "Closed," "Fix Version" vs "Affects Version," "Epic" vs "Initiative" — these distinctions matter for power users but confuse newcomers
4. **UI inconsistency**: Some screens have been redesigned (2024-2026), others are stuck in the Jira Server-era UX; the experience can feel disjointed

**What Atlassian is doing about it:**
- **Rovo-powered onboarding** (2026): New users get an AI guide that walks them through the interface based on their role
- **Simplified project templates**: "Get started in 60 seconds" templates for common team types
- **Teamwork Graph**: Visualizes how your team actually works, making it easier to spot process inefficiencies without digging through settings
- **Admin AI assistant** (Premium+): Answers "how do I..." questions about Jira configuration using natural language

### Jira vs Competitors

| Feature | Jira | Monday.com | Asana | ClickUp | Linear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Best for** | Software teams (any size) | Business teams, marketing | Cross-functional teams | All-in-one for SMBs | Speed-focused engineering teams |
| **AI agents** | Rovo agents, MCP | Monday AI | Asana Intelligence | ClickUp Brain | Linear AI |
| **Free plan** | 10 users, unlimited projects | 2 users | 10 users | Unlimited users (limited features) | 2 users |
| **Starting price (paid)** | $7.91/user/mo | $12/user/mo | $13.49/user/mo | $10/user/mo | $8/user/mo |
| **Scrum/Kanban** | Native, mature | Limited | Limited | Good | Excellent (but opinionated) |
| **Integrations** | 3,000+ | 200+ | 300+ | 1,000+ | 100+ |
| **Custom workflows** | Best in class | Good | Good | Very good | Limited (by design) |
| **Learning curve** | Steep | Moderate | Easy | Moderate | Easy |
| **API & developer tools** | Excellent (REST, MCP) | Good (GraphQL) | Good (REST) | Good (REST) | Good (GraphQL) |

**When to choose Jira over competitors:**
- You have 10+ developers building software with complex workflows
- You need AI agents that integrate with your IDE (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.)
- You require SOC 2, ISO 27001, and enterprise compliance out of the box
- Your organization already uses other Atlassian products (Confluence, Bitbucket)
- You plan to scale beyond 50 users and need advanced admin controls

**When to choose a competitor over Jira:**
- You're a non-engineering team → Monday.com or Asana
- You value speed and simplicity above all → Linear
- You want an all-in-one tool (docs + tasks + chat) → Notion or ClickUp
- You're under 10 people and want zero-config → Linear, Todoist, or Trello

### Migration and Onboarding

Moving to Jira from another tool? Atlassian provides:
- **Free migration assistants** for Trello, Asana, Monday.com, and CSV
- **Jira Cloud Migration Assistant (JCMA)** for Server/Data Center → Cloud migrations
- **Professional services** (Enterprise) for complex migrations with 1,000+ users

Expect a migration timeline of 2-4 weeks for a mid-size team (20-50 users), including:
- Week 1: Audit current process, map to Jira workflows, configure project
- Week 2: Data migration, integration setup (Slack, GitHub, CI/CD)
- Week 3: Team training, pilot project, feedback collection
- Week 4: Full rollout, workflow iteration, admin handoff

### Security and Compliance

For enterprise buyers, Jira Cloud offers:
- **SOC 2 Type II**, **ISO 27001**, **ISO 27018**, **PCI DSS Level 1**
- **GDPR** and **CCPA** compliant with data residency in US, EU, Australia, Germany, Singapore, and more
- **SAML SSO**, **SCIM** user provisioning (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin)
- **Atlassian Access** (add-on): Enforced 2FA, audit logs, API token controls, and IP allowlisting
- **Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)** encryption (Enterprise)
- **99.9% SLA** on Premium, **99.95% SLA** on Enterprise with financial penalties

Data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Atlassian's public status page (status.atlassian.com) provides real-time incident transparency, and their post-incident reviews are published publicly.

### The Verdict: Is Jira Worth It in 2026?

After evaluating Jira's 2026 feature set, pricing, and competitive landscape, here's the bottom line:

**If you're building software with a team of 10+ developers, Jira is the safe bet.** The AI agent capabilities (Rovo), MCP integration with AI coding tools, and the extensibility of the platform are unmatched. The learning curve is real, but the 2026 onboarding improvements — AI-guided setup, workflow templates, and the Teamwork Graph — meaningfully reduce the initial friction.

**If you're a small startup (under 10 people)** with engineering talent that values speed, try Linear first. If you outgrow it, Jira's free tier is waiting for you with a clear upgrade path.

**If you're a non-engineering team**, you will likely be happier with Monday.com or Asana, which were built for your use case from day one.

**Jira's biggest risk in 2026** isn't competition — it's itself. The platform's power is also its liability. Without disciplined administration, Jira instances accumulate technical debt just like codebases: custom fields nobody uses, workflows with dead-end statuses, permission schemes that nobody can untangle. If your organization can commit to a **Jira admin role** (even part-time), the investment pays off. If you can't, the tool will eventually work against you.

**Final Score: 94/100** — The gold standard for software project management, now powered by AI agents that meaningfully reduce toil. Deducted points for the learning curve and UI clutter that still need work.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Jira and who is it for?

Jira is a project management and issue-tracking platform by Atlassian, purpose-built for software development teams. It supports Scrum, Kanban, and hybrid methodologies with customizable workflows, AI-powered automation, and 3,000+ integrations. It's used by over 300,000 organizations worldwide — from 5-person startups to Fortune 50 enterprises like NASA, Tesla, and Airbnb.

### Is Jira really free for 10 users?

Yes. Jira's Free plan includes unlimited goals, projects, tasks, backlog, Scrum and Kanban boards, timeline and calendar views, 100 automation rule runs per month, and 2 GB of storage — free forever for up to 10 users. No credit card is required to sign up. There's no time limit; the Free plan isn't a trial.

### How much does Jira cost for a team of 20?

For a 20-person team on Standard (monthly billing): $7.91 × 20 = **$158.20/month** ($1,898.40/year). On Premium (annual billing): $12.10 × 20 = **$242/month** ($2,904/year). The Free plan is not available for teams over 10 users. If your team is exactly 20, Standard is the most common choice unless you need cross-team planning and 24/7 support.

### What are Rovo AI agents in Jira?

Rovo AI agents are Atlassian's autonomous AI assistants that operate within Jira projects. They can auto-triage incoming bugs, generate sprint retrospectives from commit and PR data, identify duplicate issues, suggest story point estimates, and auto-assign tasks based on developer expertise and workload. Rovo agents are included from the Standard plan upward. They are not simple chatbots — they take action within your Jira instance (transitioning issues, assigning users, generating reports) with configurable permission scopes.

### What is Jira MCP and why does it matter for developers?

Jira's MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration allows AI coding assistants — including Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and GitHub Copilot — to read and update Jira issues directly from the terminal or IDE. For example, a developer can type a natural language command in Claude Code to transition a Jira ticket, add a comment with a PR link, or query the status of sprint work — all without leaving their coding environment. This eliminates context switching and is estimated to save 2-5 hours per developer per week on Jira administrative tasks.

### How does Jira compare to Monday.com?

Jira is purpose-built for software development with deep Scrum/Kanban support, custom workflows, and developer tool integrations (GitHub, CI/CD, MCP for AI coding tools). Monday.com is a more general-purpose work management platform with a friendlier UI, better suited for marketing, HR, and operations teams. Jira wins on depth and flexibility for engineering teams; Monday.com wins on ease of use and visual appeal for non-technical teams. Jira's free tier (10 users) is more generous than Monday.com's (2 users).

### How does Jira compare to Linear?

Linear is Jira's most credible competitor for speed-focused engineering teams. Linear prioritizes a clean, keyboard-driven interface with opinionated workflows that enforce good practices by default. Jira prioritizes flexibility — you can configure it to work however your team works. Linear is faster to set up and more pleasant to use day-to-day; Jira is more powerful for complex, multi-team organizations with compliance requirements. If your team is under 30 engineers and values speed over configurability, try Linear. If you're scaling beyond that or need enterprise compliance, Jira is the safer choice.

### How does Jira compare to Asana?

Asana offers a more intuitive, visually polished experience with strong project management features for cross-functional teams (marketing, design, operations, and engineering working together). Jira is deeper for pure software development — custom workflows, Scrum/Kanban boards, sprint management, and developer tool integrations are all more mature. Asana's AI features (Asana Intelligence) focus on project health predictions and workload management; Jira's Rovo AI focuses on developer productivity (auto-generating PR descriptions, triaging bugs, estimating story points).

### Can Jira be used for non-software projects?

Yes, but it's not ideal. Jira's architecture, terminology (epics, sprints, story points), and feature set are built around software development. Teams in marketing, HR, legal, or operations can use Jira — and Atlassian has introduced templates for these use cases — but tools like Monday.com, Asana, or ClickUp typically provide a better out-of-the-box experience for non-technical workflows. If your entire organization runs on Atlassian (Jira + Confluence), running non-engineering projects in Jira makes sense for consistency. Otherwise, choose a tool built for your team type.

### Is Jira secure for enterprise use?

Yes. Jira Cloud is SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27018, and PCI DSS Level 1 certified. It offers SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, enforced 2FA via Atlassian Access, IP allowlisting, BYOK encryption (Enterprise), and data residency options in multiple regions (US, EU, Australia, Germany, Singapore). The Enterprise plan includes a 99.95% uptime SLA. All data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).

### What happens when the Jira free trial ends?

The Free plan is not a trial — it's free forever for up to 10 users. Standard and Premium plans offer a 7-day free trial; when the trial ends, you're automatically billed unless you cancel. You can downgrade to Free at any time, though you'll lose access to features like Rovo AI, advanced roadmaps, and custom roles.

### Does Jira have a mobile app?

Yes, Jira has iOS and Android apps. The mobile app supports viewing and creating issues, approving or rejecting transitions, commenting, and receiving push notifications. However, the mobile experience is limited compared to desktop — you can't configure workflows, manage automation rules, or use advanced search (JQL) effectively. It's best for triaging and quick updates on the go, not for deep work.

mainEntity.name: Can Jira be used for non-software projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but it's not ideal. Jira's architecture, terminology (epics, sprints, story points), and feature set are built around software development. Teams in marketing, HR, legal, or operations can use Jira — and Atlassian has introduced templates for these use cases — but tools like Monday.com, Asana, or ClickUp typically provide a better out-of-the-box experience for non-technical workflows.

mainEntity.name: Is Jira secure for enterprise use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Jira Cloud is SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27018, and PCI DSS Level 1 certified. It offers SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, enforced 2FA via Atlassian Access, IP allowlisting, BYOK encryption (Enterprise), and data residency options in the US, EU, Australia, Germany, and Singapore. The Enterprise plan includes a 99.95% uptime SLA. All data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).

mainEntity.name: What happens when the Jira free trial ends?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Free plan is not a trial — it's free forever for up to 10 users. Standard and Premium plans offer a 7-day free trial; when the trial ends, you're automatically billed unless you cancel. You can downgrade to Free at any time, though you'll lose access to features like Rovo AI, advanced roadmaps, and custom roles.

mainEntity.name: Does Jira have a mobile app?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Jira has iOS and Android apps that support viewing and creating issues, approving transitions, commenting, and receiving push notifications. However, the mobile experience is limited compared to desktop — you can't configure workflows, manage automation rules, or use advanced JQL search effectively. It's best for triaging and quick updates on the go, not for deep work.

mainEntity.name: How does Jira compare to Asana?

acceptedAnswer.text: Asana offers a more intuitive, visually polished experience with strong project management features for cross-functional teams. Jira is deeper for pure software development — custom workflows, Scrum/Kanban boards, sprint management, and developer tool integrations are all more mature. Asana's AI (Asana Intelligence) focuses on project health predictions; Jira's Rovo AI focuses on developer productivity like auto-generating PR descriptions and triaging bugs.
